items.title: New alloy design strategy combines strength and ductility by timing hardening mechanisms
items.summary: Structural metals used in engineering projects are expected to have both high strength and high ductility: the ability to withstand heavy loads and deform before failure. Achieving both of these properties at the same time, however, is challenging.

items.title: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
items.summary: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

items.title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
items.summary: Mixed ionic–electronic conductors (MIECs) are highly desirable for a wide range of electronic applications, however, developing single-phase MIECs with intrinsic transport properties under ambient conditions remains challenging.
items.source: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title: First bacterial galactose oxidase expands toolkit for greener drug and food ingredient production
items.summary: To produce pharmaceuticals, food ingredients, and flavors and fragrances, it is often necessary to oxidize alcohols. In conventional chemistry, this transformation typically relies on harsh oxidants and elevated temperatures and generates toxic waste.

items.title: Autonomous Biogenesis of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
items.summary: Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction.
items.source: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.title: Separable downmodulation of meiotic axis protein deposition and DNA break induction at chromosome ends
items.summary: In many organisms, meiotic crossover recombination is suppressed near the extreme ends of chromosomes. Here we show that multiple, often chromosome-specific, suppressive mechanisms with differing ranges contribute to the consistently low enrichment of recombination-promoting axis proteins and downregulation of DNA double-strand breaks…

items.title: New drug-delivery method offers promise in fight against neurodegenerative diseases
items.summary: For patients battling neurodegenerative diseases like ALS, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and other dementias, delivering disease-fighting antibody drugs directly to the brain has proven to be a difficult task. Our bodies set up tight walls to prevent infections from spreading to the brain, where they often become fatal.

items.title: Part 1 of a 2-part, open-label clinical trial evaluating repeated nicotinamide riboside parenteral administration: 3 consecutive days of intramuscular and subcutaneous injections
items.summary: Nicotinamide riboside (NR), an endogenous precursor to the essential coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), is characterized as safe and effective for longitudinally elevating NAD+ in blood and tissues, when administered orally.

items.title: Placebo-Adjusted Frequencies of Nonserious Adverse Reactions Listed on US Prescription Drug Labels
items.summary: Importance: Drug labels list adverse reactions with their frequency among patients receiving the drug, which is commonly read as the risk added by the drug. Objective:: To compare drug and placebo frequencies of nonserious adverse reactions listed on current US Food and Drug Administration labels, using placebo-controlled randomized…

items.title: Study finds differences in cellular responses to exercise
items.summary: A recently published study by University of New Mexico researchers looks at how intense exercise affects the body. Michael Deyhle, an associate professor in the Department of Health, Exercise and Sports Sciences, oversaw the study led by doctoral students Jonathan Specht, Jeremy Ducharme and Alyssa Bailly.

items.title: Stronger Through the Transition: Evaluating the Effect of Creatine and Resistance Training on Body Composition, Strength, and Sleep in Perimenopause
items.summary: HIRT improved muscle outcomes, with CM adding 0.38 kg to LST and 148.6 lbs to strength.

items.title: Blood Flow Restriction Training in Older Adults with Cancer: Rationale, Clinical Applications and Future Perspectives
items.summary: Cancer predominantly affects older adults, who frequently present with frailty, sarcopenia, cachexia, multimorbidity, and functional decline that limit tolerance to conventional exercise interventions.

items.title: Inflammation is already elevated at the earliest stage of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome
items.summary: A new analysis of U.S. national health data finds that high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a blood marker of inflammation, rises across the stages of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, with the largest increase at the earliest stage.

items.title: Empagliflozin Improves Muscle Weakness in a Patient with Suspected Glycogen Storage Myopathy: A Case Report
items.summary: Objective To describe the clinical course of a patient with chronic progressive muscle weakness and intramyocellular glycogen deposition who received empagliflozin. Methods We present a case of a young male patient with chronic progressive proximal limb weakness, exercise intolerance, and supine dyspnea.

items.title: Body data could provide a 24-hour warning for headaches
items.summary: Some people who suffer a concussion struggle with headaches and fatigue afterward. These symptoms follow a consistent pattern that could be used to warn the patient a full day before they set in.

items.title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
items.summary: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe…

items.title: Reversing age by reprogramming gene expression networks
items.summary: Every organ and tissue progressively loses function and integrity as it ages. In fact, researchers have identified "hallmarks of aging" that not only present specific processes impacted by age, but are also thought of as levers that, if successfully targeted, could help turn back the aging clock and result in tissue rejuvenation.

items.title: Tennis Participation Across the Lifespan: Functional and Biological Adaptations Relevant to Healthy Aging
items.summary: Maintaining physiological function, mobility, and independence throughout aging remains a major challenge in exercise and health sciences. Physical activity is widely recognized as a key determinant of healthy aging, yet different sports may confer distinct biological benefits.

items.title: Lone, starless cloud may be a 'dark' galaxy
items.summary: Astronomers using China's FAST radio telescope have discovered a compact cloud of hydrogen with no visible stars or galaxy around it. This could be one of the strongest candidates yet for an isolated "dark galaxy," containing nearly 500,000 times the sun's mass in neutral hydrogen.

items.title: Laboratory Measurements of Energy Partitioning and Anomalous Electron Heating in Magnetized, Perpendicular Collisionless Shocks
items.summary: We present laboratory results on energy partitioning from supercritical, magnetized collisionless shock experiments ( M A ∼ 8, M ms ∼ 4). We report the first observation of fully developed laboratory shocks that evolve for more than seven upstream ion gyroperiods and have a downstream region that extends for more than four shocked ion…

items.title: Can social media bans protect young people's mental health? Early research suggests that bans aren't the answer
items.summary: The year 2026 has been an expensive one for social media platforms. Since March, YouTube and Meta, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, have settled or paid out in multiple lawsuits totaling more than $17 billion for allegedly acting negligently, deliberately designing their platforms to hook kids and misleading the public about…

items.title: Essential oil sprays kill cockroaches on contact but offer little lasting control
items.summary: A German cockroach races across a kitchen floor. Someone grabs a bottle of essential oil spray, soaks the insect and watches it die. The product worked, but a new University of Kentucky study suggests the larger infestation probably did not notice.

items.title: Using AI to help find Mexico's legions of missing children
items.summary: Veronica Rosas is one of tens of thousands of Mexican mothers looking for a child who has disappeared into a vortex of violence fueled by brutal cartel turf wars.
